findings.expected: every element that takes keyboard focus exposes a non-empty accessible name
reproduction: show the shelf with F2
press Tab through one complete cycle and read the name of the FOCUSED element after each press
findings.minimal_fix: the focusable element is the GtkScrolledWindow the host wraps each list in; GTK leaves its accessible unnamed while it still takes focus, so name it in reader.c: atk_object_set_name(gtk_widget_get_accessible(gtk_widget_get_ancestor(image, GTK_TYPE_SCROLLED_WINDOW)), "Page") and the same for the shelf, notes, organizer group and member lists

findings.expected: the organizer is a modal dialog named 'Library collections' with keyboard focus inside it
reproduction: open the organizer from the shelf more menu with the keyboard
read the dialog element and the focused element
findings.minimal_fix: GTK_DIALOG_MODAL is already requested, but GTK never moves focus into the dialog: add gtk_widget_grab_focus(collections.types) (or collections.groups) after gtk_widget_show_all in collections_open(), as metadata_present() and accounts_open() already do

findings.expected: the collection type selector can be reached from the keyboard, either in the Tab cycle or through its mnemonic
reproduction: open the organizer
Tab through one complete cycle, then press Alt+T
read the focused element after each step
findings.minimal_fix: the selector sits outside the Tab chain and is reachable only through its _Type mnemonic; add gtk_widget_set_can_focus(collections.types, TRUE) while keeping the mnemonic widget so both paths work

findings.expected: every shelf row exposes a non-empty accessible name so list navigation can announce the book
reproduction: import originals, show the shelf with F2
read the Name property of each list row on the bus
findings.minimal_fix: in reader.c shelf_present(), after building the caption: atk_object_set_name(gtk_widget_get_accessible(row), caption) before the row is inserted; one call per row and no layout change. The caption is only reachable today as a child label, which a reader may fall back to but which leaves the row Name empty for AT-SPI clients that use it

text_children: Audit note for the GTK accessibility audit

reproduction: select page text with F7 then ctrl+a
type a comment after F11
press F8 to add the note
read the saved-note rows
findings.minimal_fix: in reader.c notes_present(), after gtk_label_new(result->notes[i].text): atk_object_set_name(gtk_widget_get_accessible(row), result->notes[i].text) for the created row

findings.expected: a refused import changes the status element name in place and the registry delivers an accessible-name property change for it

actual.after_text: Reading operation failed; accepted page retained

reproduction: read the status label name
import invalid.epub with F1
read the label again and the delivered accessibility events
findings.minimal_fix: the message is a plain label: use a GtkStatusbar (ATK_ROLE_STATUSBAR plus Statusbar::text-pushed) so assistive clients that announce status bars receive the change; GTK3 has no per-widget live region

findings.expected: the account dialog declares the MODAL state, as the organizer and details dialogs do, so assistive clients can announce that the library is unavailable while it is open

actual.main_window_sensitive_note: accounts_open() sets the main content insensitive instead of asking GTK for a modal dialog

reproduction: press Ctrl+Shift+A
read the dialog state set on the accessibility bus
findings.minimal_fix: pass GTK_DIALOG_MODAL to gtk_dialog_new_with_buttons in accounts_open() (accounts_ui.inc); the insensitive main content can then stay or go

findings.expected: Escape closes the account dialog and focus returns to a control inside the main window
reproduction: open Account and Sync
press Escape
read the focused element
findings.minimal_fix: accounts_open() makes the whole main content insensitive, which drops the main window focus widget, and accounts_destroyed() only re-enables it: remember the focused widget before opening and grab it again in accounts_destroyed(), or use GTK_DIALOG_MODAL instead of insensitivity

gaps: Orca or any real screen reader speech output (no speech capture, no reader build)
AT-SPI live-region / announcement semantics: the audited GTK3 host sets no live region attribute and at-spi2-core on the runner predates object:announcement
Braille display output and BRLTTY integration
Visible focus ring, contrast and theme rendering (WCAG 1.4.3/1.4.11/2.4.7)
Password-field semantics at the AT-SPI layer: GTK3 exports no password attribute, so an assistive client cannot be told that the field is secret before reading it
IME composition, caret browsing and selection announcement for the rendered page image
Network-backed account scan states (preparing, scanning, cancel, retry) because this audit runs offline against a local library only
Non-GTK hosts: Windows, Apple and Android surfaces are outside this package
Event coalescing and AT-SPI cache latency under a large library

remaining_work: Orca or any real screen-reader speech pass is not granted: it needs a reader run with speech capture, which this package does not perform.
Six blocking findings are host defects: the GTK receiver owns reader.c and accounts_ui.inc and must decide the fixes listed in findings[].minimal_fix.
The organizer type selector stays outside the Tab cycle (advisory) and its mnemonic probe is inconclusive until the dialog takes initial focus.
Network-backed account scan states (preparing, scanning, cancel, retry) remain uncovered because the audit runs offline.
Windows, Apple and Android surfaces are outside this package.
Braille output, contrast/theme rendering, IME and caret browsing are recorded as gaps, not as passes.
